APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL ADJOURNED REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 8, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:05 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  SPECIALLY ADDED AGENDA ITEM:

  CLOSED SESSION ITEM:

  4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  (e)(5) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Receipt of
  Correspondence Threatening Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Councilmember Velasco  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION (6:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m.):

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond
  such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized
  Closed Session matter pursuant to the Brown Act (Govt. Code Section 54950 et seq.).

  Mayor Quintero invited members of the public to address the City Council on
  Closed Session Items 4.1 through 4.4.

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at
  approximately 6:06 p.m.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 8, 2019

  Mayor Quintero and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:00 p.m.

  City Attorney Rick Olivarez reported out of Closed Session with respect to Items

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  David Reynoso, Chief of Police. Present

   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 8, 2019

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS: No
  Material Submitted.

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.
  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Edward Barrera – State Senator Susan Rubio would like to cordially invite the Council as
  well as members of the public to her swearing in this Saturday from 10:30 am to 11:30
  am at the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse located at 320 S. Mission Drive, San Gabriel.
  If you need more information or you want to rsvp please contact (626) 430-2499. I also
  left some flyers there both in English and Spanish. I hope to see some of you there.

  Gabriel Ramirez – I just want to say Happy New Year to those that are hear. I know that
  on December 18th there was an incident outside as I have been hearing one of our
  activist and advocate and was also a former School Board Member who ran for
  Mountain View. Irma Zamorano was attacked by a pro cannabis protestor and
  unfortunately she was in the hospital and a couple of days later she was released. If you
  don’t agree with the issues there is no place and need for violence this is something that
  has been happening.

  Rebecca Urac– Have been working for the Sanitation Districts for almost 19 years. I am
  a member who has been speaking on behalf of nearly 1,000 fellow employees across
  the six bargaining units of the Sanitation Districts. The reason I am here is that the
  Sanitation Districts is embroiled in a labor management turmoil and our long standing
  impasses and negotiations can spill over to the communities that we serve. The
  Sanitation Districts negotiating team is attempting to cut our total compensation. We
  have been through both mediation and fact finding. The fact finder confirmed that

  3
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 8, 2019

  Districts can afford what we are asking for. I am asking that you send a letter to the
  Sanitation Districts Senior Management to withdraw this unreasonable proposal.

  Eduardo Almeda Salceda – I want to thank the City Council, Mr. Andre Quintero on his
  election for Mayor I was very pleased that one of the Councilmembers called me to invite
  me to a small get together. As you know we got a new City Clerk and I would like to
  welcome him to the Sister City of South El Monte.

12.  CONSENT CALENDAR:

  All matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine in nature and
  may be enacted by one motion approving the recommendation listed on the Agenda.
  One or more items may be removed from the Consent Calendar so that they may be
  discussed, considered and voted upon individually by the Council. A matter may be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and taken up separately by way of a seconded
  motion of any member of the Council with the approval of a majority of the Council
  quorum.

  12.1  Approval for Second Reading of an Uncodified Ordinance Approving: (1)
  Development Agreement No. 02-18 with GSC Holding Group, LLC for the
  Commercial Cultivation, Manufacturing, and Distribution of Medicinal Cannabis at
  4400 Temple City Boulevard, El Monte, California; and (2) a Mitigated Negative
  Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program as the
  Environmental Documentation for such Project.
  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Ratify the proposed Ordinance by second reading by at least three (3)
  affirmative votes.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2939

  Diane Cheung – I am so glad you are having another hearing again and you didn’t build
  anything yet. My sentiment is to oppose I know people have different opinions and
  different believes I don’t support building the proposed project. One student told me her
  step father uses the drug and he can’t stop using it. I have another student who said that
  her brother started using drugs too.

  Terence Vuong – I support medical marijuana my friend was diagnosed last year with lip
  sarcoma and because of medical marijuana he was able to relieve some of his pain.

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 8, 2019

Ke-Wei Zhao – I am resident of El Monte and I want to congratulate the new elected
members. I oppose the building of the marijuana facilities. In the short run it can get the
City revenue but in the long run it will hurt the City it will hurt the environment. It will hurt
the safety of the community. I ask the members to vote no on Item 12.1.

Qiang Bjornbak – I stand here before you to cordially request the Mayor and the Council
to reconsider this project because it is too close to the neighborhood and to close to the
school areas. The California records show that at the 4352 Temple City Boulevard the
site is heavily contaminated by heavy metals and organic matter for many years. I
wonder if the City can do its due diligence at 4400 Temple City Boulevard to see if it is
also contaminated so that it is not the proper site for cannabis grow.

Speaker (no name) – I came here to share a little bit about cannabis marijuana as I
know that recently the State passed marijuana legally. A lot of accidents happen outside
on the City streets and freeway because of DUI. I oppose marijuana in this City. I have
been living here for more than 40 years and I want this City to be safe for everyone.

Norma Morfin – As a Latina I would like to speak in Spanish to represent the entire
Hispanic community and I am against what is happening in the City of El Monte and I am
against marijuana and you want to put it in locations where the schools are right next to
it and I think it is unjust.

Sam Meng – Although I am a resident of Rowland Heights I am very concerned about
this issue and I represent part of the Greater Los Angeles Communities Alliance where
many of our El Monte residents are members also. I want to put into words the feelings
of the community. This isn’t just stigma but the experience of what happened because of
opium. The City Council should appreciate the extra view point of the Chinese
community. Although marijuana is legal according to federal law no matter how much is
mitigated there are some things that you can’t protect.

Feng Lan Luu – I submitted a proposal on behalf of 20,000 residents from El Monte and
Temple City. I have a chart here this is a report from the Department of Toxic Substance
Control from this Department a report was made in 2017 certain acres were
contaminated I want to know why City of El Monte on 6.9 acres were followed by this
report and why other 6 acres were never cleaned up.

Alan Zhong – I live in El Monte I want to share a story when an elementary school guy
when I collected the signatures a boy knows what I was collecting for so he told his
mother what it was for and he told us his school is very close to this medical cannabis
facility and him and all his classmates are against it.

Jathan Peery – I am here to support the applicant and to speak about the contamination
on the site and the area in general. The VOCs are basically contaminous and have
been in the San Gabriel Valley for a very very long time since the 50s and in 1979 they
came in and entered the aquafer which is where we get all of the water for the San
Gabriel Valley that serves more than 2,000,000 residents. What we are doing at the site
is that we are actively cleaning it. We have been cleaning it up we spent approximately
$360,000 already to clean up this site so that those VOCs that are in the soil do not
enter the groundwater. It is an on-going progress.

Speaker 13 – I want to please vote no because I want my children safe and the air clear.

Jenny Zhang – I am an El Monte resident and I live next to the library. I protest this
marijuana project because it will pollute our land and our environment. There are 13
acres of land contaminated by metal and organic matter for many years. The California
Toxic Substance Authority asked owners to clean up years ago but it has failed to do so
for more than a decade. Our volunteer have repeatedly asked for more information and
they have been denied access to it and now El Monte Councilmen are going to approve
the establishment of a marijuana base here but we must not allow such outrageous
project to be carried out.

Richard Chow – I am a resident of El Monte I didn’t prepare a speech but on behalf of
my neighborhood and my community we live in a fair and decent community. Cannabis
has been legalized but we don’t know about the side effects. About our safety the toxic
cleaning in the near future it will cost a lot of money. We still have the law conflict with
the federal. How about we wait for the final no more conflict with federal law.

  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 8, 2019

  Dr. K. Huang – I have been a medical doctor for some forty something years. I have
  seen nothing good about marijuana and people know about that. But shouldn’t you pass
  that ordinance and which comply with State of California even Jerry Brown signed it too
  in January of 2018 so I not opposing because I know it is no use because your
  honorable body sitting up there passed your rules already but I want you to listen to the
  people what they are concerned about. In this particular group you see most of them I
  would say Asians, Chinese Americans of course a few residents talk over here. Their
  concern should concern about you.

  Brief break at 7:35 pm
  Returned at 7:44 pm

  Miu – I have been working in the ICU as an RN for many years. I strongly oppose the
  plan to build marijuana production center in the City of El Monte. I am not against the
  medical marijuana. I took care of patients with marijuana user I just had a patient died in
  the ICU and when you talk about the job opportunity and the taxation.

  Charles Hoffman – I am against marijuana but I am in favor of medical cannabis. This
  project is all to do with medical cannabis it will be done in a building inside the building
  not outside and it is negative draft. People that are speaking have not read or know the
  City Code that knows that this project meets all codes that the City has set. It is a good
  project and hopefully it will bring some revenue into the City. I am for this project.

  Eden Chien – I speak on behalf of residents in the City and satellite cities. I oppose this
  project because it will break many people’s American dream. Many people from all over
  the world and they were here to pursue the American Dream but because of this plan it
  will relable the City as a drug city that grow marijuana and sell and distribute. It will
  cause many people to move out of El Monte. I urge everyone to reconsider this project
  because it will empty out this neighborhood not only El Monte.

  Ken Meng – I am from Rowland Heights and I oppose the project because I know from
  the Chinese history marijuana is a drug and it will damage people it is harmful. I think all
  of you guys need to think how to care for your citizens if it is simply about money you
  can probably get it from somewhere else instead of this. You can see that there are
  many people protesting and on January 4th we had a press conference and I am going to
  email the video to you so you can enjoy it.

  Joe Meng – I am also from Rowland Heights so my concern about this project is the
  normalization of marijuana. Everyone knows that this legalization is very powerful and
  they are pushing the benefits that it brings to the community and I want to say that it is
  very detrimental because marijuana is a drug. We have seen many people who are
  addicted to marijuana and this project will accelerate the normalization and bring another
  wave of something like the opioid crisis that happened earlier. Marijuana we still have a
  chance to keep it out of the hands of kids because it is not engrained in our society like
  tobacco and alcohol.

  Yan Lee – I have lived in El Monte for 20 years. I oppose this project because marijuana
  will make our City very bad I hope you can stop it.

  m) Mayor Quintero

  13.1  Consideration and Approval of (1) an Urgency Ordinance Amending Chapter

  Small Wireless Facilities; and (2) a Resolution Implementing Special Provisions
  for Small Wireless Facilities Pursuant to the Report and Order and Declaratory

  September 28, 2018.

Erin Schnider – I work from Crown Castle a wireless infrastructure provider the largest in the
country and we work with the major wireless providers obviously this Ordinance is of paramount
importance to me. I am the Project Manager for the company who builds in this area. I have
about 80 applications that I would like to submit to the City in the next month and there are
couple of items I would like to discuss within the context of the amendment that are of concern
to me. We are moving away from traditional towers to small cell antennas to things that are
mounted to cable lines. There is a limitation in this ordinance that we need to keep this to one
cubic foot and from a technical perspective we can’t do that. There is also a preference about
the types of zones that we are supposed to be building in from commercial areas to residential
as well as a setback of 250 feet from residential structures. The problem is that we are building
now to fit residential demand the code as it sits provides a tiered amount of restrictions there
which inhibits our ability to quickly deploy these types of facilities.

18B.  Councilwoman Ancona

  I hope you all enjoyed your winter break or the holidays I had winter break I don’t
  know about the rest of you but as we are back now I am really looking forward to

  Pro Temship I would like to see if maybe we can establish a Resolution that kind
  of sets this rotation in place and sets a criteria in an effort to codify how this is

  and collegiality here on the City Council and I would like to hopefully see in the
  upcoming meetings on the agenda and that is all thank you.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Can I just piggy back on that very quickly.

18C.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  Piggybacking years ago we had attempted to have a rotating Mayor based on the
  same criteria of either seniority or if there were two members that joined at the
  same time that it would be the person who received more votes in that election
  cycle. And unfortunately the Mayor ship didn’t happen at that point and the Mayor
  rotating Mayor vote to the people did not happen but I hope that in this dais it will
  and that there is a certain date that would be set so that it automatically rotates
  so that there is no politicizing that it is simply a process and procedure and it
  really doesn’t need to go to those levels. In fact, in an effort of true collegiality it
  would just continue to join this particular Council in a positive movement forward.
  We are going to be getting together this Saturday in regards to a Council
  workshop working on our priorities and for the community I want you to know that
  this Council isn’t going to stop working on your behalf. We have some big ideas
  and big dreams and little dollars so we need to really make sure that we are
  conscientious of the realities of serving this City at this particular time. It isn’t
  overflowing in funds, in fact we are operating in dire straits and we want to make
  sure that we can continue to provide you the safest, cleanest and just well
  programmed City so that you and your family can live, work and raise a family
  here. So I hope that you did have a wonderful New Year and I look forward to a
